content:
Apple has further revealed more details about the Apple Music AI labelling rules announced earlier this March. Here's what you need to know.

AI-generated content will be clearly labelled on Apple Music

Apple previously announced that Apple Music would require cover art, songs, tracks and music videos newly submitted to the platform to disclose AI transparency information.

Now, Apple has further explained how this practice will work.

In an email sent to creators today, Apple stated: "Later this year, we will also display this notification to Apple Music listeners in the form of a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple has also clarified when disclosure is required. The email reads as follows:

Apple Music added that the goal of this measure is to "provide maximum transparency to listeners as much as possible", and asked creators to refer to their Style Guide for more information.

Apple Music's approach is just the latest example of streaming platforms responding to the proliferation of AI-generated music, as more and more musicians begin incorporating generative AI into their production workflows.

Spotify previously said that, by default, music from AI personas would be excluded from editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer also announced last year that fully AI-generated tracks would not receive recommendations or be included in editorial playlists. Deezer also revealed last month that fully AI-generated music has for the first time surpassed 50% of newly uploaded songs daily.

On the Apple Music front, platform head Oliver Schusser previously appeared on Billboard's *On the Record* podcast, noting that although more than one-third of music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of the platform's listening volume.
